name: azure_key_vault_secret
description: Manages a secret inside an Azure Key Vault. Key Vault secrets are append-only: writing a name that already exists adds a new version rather than overwriting the old one, so any change here produces a new version and a new `version` value. The secret's value is write-only — the API never returns it, only its metadata.

notFoundResponses.messagePattern: ^Secret '[^']+' was not found in Key Vault '[^']+'

attributes.name: workspace_id
attributes.description: Workspace that owns the vault (path parameter).

attributes.name: key_vault_id
attributes.description: Backend id of the Key Vault holding this secret — the `vault_record_id` of a duploai_azure_key_vault, not the ARM resource id (path parameter).

attributes.name: name
attributes.description: Secret name, unique within the vault. Letters, numbers and hyphens only. Changing it creates a different secret, so the old one is destroyed — and Azure keeps a deleted name reserved in a recoverable state until it is purged or recovered.

attributes.name: value
attributes.description: Secret value. One of `value` or `value_wo` is required — the API rejects a create without one. The API never returns it, so the configured value is kept in Terraform state and a change made outside Terraform cannot be detected. Because Key Vault is append-only, sending a value creates a new version even when it is unchanged, and the platform cannot update a secret's metadata without a value, so the value is sent on every update — every update (including a tags- or `content_type`-only change) creates a new secret version.

attributes.name: value_wo
attributes.description: Write-only alternative to `value`, for Terraform 1.11 and later: the value is sent to the API but never stored in the plan or state. Set `value_wo_version` with it, and change `value_wo_version` whenever this value changes — Terraform cannot see a change to a write-only value, so the version change is what plans the update that sends it. On Terraform earlier than 1.11, use `value` instead. Only one of the two may be set. Choose one field per configuration: a conditional on a variable that sets one or the other fails validation, because Terraform validates before variable values are known. Key Vault is append-only and the platform cannot update a secret's metadata without a value, so — exactly like `value` — this value is sent on every update, and every update creates a new secret version.

attributes.name: value_wo_version
attributes.description: Version of `value_wo`. Required when `value_wo` is set. The value itself is arbitrary (1, 2, 3, …): changing it sends the current `value_wo` on the next apply. Stored in state; the secret is not.

attributes.name: content_type
attributes.description: Free-form hint describing what the value holds, e.g. "text/plain" or "application/json". Azure does not interpret it.

attributes.name: enabled
attributes.description: Whether the secret can be read. Disabling keeps the secret and its versions but makes reads fail. Defaults to enabled.

attributes.name: expires_on
attributes.description: When the secret stops being valid, as an RFC 3339 timestamp. Azure does not delete an expired secret — reads simply fail. Leave unset for no expiry.

attributes.name: not_before
attributes.description: When the secret becomes valid, as an RFC 3339 timestamp. Reads before this time fail. Leave unset to make it valid immediately.

attributes.name: tags
attributes.description: Free-form key/value tags on the secret.

attributes.name: secret_id
attributes.description: Full Azure identifier of this secret version, e.g. https://my-vault.vault.azure.net/secrets/db-password/<version>.

attributes.name: version
attributes.description: Identifier of the current version. Changes every time a value is written, including when the value is unchanged.

attributes.name: created_on
attributes.description: When this version was created (RFC 3339, normalized to UTC at second precision).

attributes.name: updated_on
attributes.description: When this version was last updated (RFC 3339, normalized to UTC at second precision).
